impact_parameter: distance from the origin to each ray. Native: from the sphere point. Reference: from the observation-plane crossing (x, y, 0) of the same ray (IACT convention)

mapping.geometry: telescope sphere radius 15 m at origin, viewing cone 10 deg about (0,0,-1), altitude 2150 m (both)
mapping.spectrum: fixed 400 nm (both); inside the 300-650 nm band of the configured rate
mapping.rate: configured 0.24 ph/(sr ns cm^2) (nsbls help text) -> photons per event = rate x Omega x pi R^2 x window
mapping.window: uniform pulse of FWHM 2.35482 ns, i.e. width 1 ns (both)
mapping.time_convention: native compared at the sphere centre plane, t - (X.d)/c; reference IACT time + event time_offset
mapping.atmosphere: nsbls -A 1 and obdeect -A 1 (recorded; profile for air speed only)
mapping.sim_telarray: propagate --no-extinction then obdeect stream to-simtel; telescope_theta=0, trigger_telescopes=1

physics_limits.yield_and_rate: max(0.01, 5 se) with se=0: fixed photon count per event in both
physics_limits.projected_area: isotropic flux is uniform in projected area on the sphere (rho^2 uniform); KS alpha=1e-3
physics_limits.camera: max(0.01, 5 se) on the relative p.e. per event ratio (task rule)

reproducibility: nsbls has no seed option: the reference sample is not reproducible; the native run is seeded (17)
limit_setting: Limits set before the first run. The projected-area check is an analytic check of the declared isotropic flux (rho^2 uniform). Native impact parameters follow the declared sampler (1 - sqrt(U), KS passes); the flux is not area-uniform, and nsbls differs from obdeect (KS 0.18).
camera_status: BLOCKED: camera comparison needs at least two triggered events per sample; sim_telarray triggered events: native 0, reference 0
